[ 02 ] HOW IT WORKS

Three deterministic stages.
One human gate.

10.8 ms DETERMINISTIC BURST SCAN · 1,000 MSGS
STAGE 01

One grouped incident instead of 25 separate alerts.

When 5+ accounts repeat identical spam inside 10 seconds, spam.py freezes the target list and strips URLs and emails before Switch sees a byte.

WINDOW=10.0s · THRESHOLD=5+ ACCOUNTS · INC-001=6 LOCKED
0 auto-bans HARD HUMAN GATE IN #STREAM-OPS
STAGE 02

AI drafts the batch. Only your moderator closes the circuit.

ban_user and delete_message stay permanently in approve mode. Viewing locks targets; mismatching --count rejects execution.

@crew-mod: pending #1 · 6 accounts · [link removed]
$ crew approve 1 --count 6 --by Sam
WAITING FOR --BY ATTRIBUTION · AIR GAP OPEN
0.5 s HELIX PACING · 25-TARGET CAP
STAGE 03

Sequential dispatch that never trips rate limits.

Once approved, the local worker sends one Helix timeout every 0.5 seconds, records the moderator name in SQLite, and keeps DRY_RUN=true by default.

HELIX QUEUE · 6 / 6 TIMED OUT · 3.0 s ELAPSED
audit_log: approval_id=1 · action=timeout_user · by=Sam
/overlay UPDATED · SUMMARY ONLY

    [ 04 ] WHY IT EXISTS

    Raids move faster than one moderator.

    In 2021, coordinated hate raids hit Twitch faster than any moderator could type ban commands. StreamCrew turns a flood into one decision and a permanent record.

    [ 04B ] ARCHITECTURE

    Why Switch is essential:
    separation of powers.

    A local script serves one operator. Switch splits observation, drafting, and execution across human and agent roles.

    01 · ROLE BOUNDARIES SWITCH ROOM · #stream-ops

    Two Humans & Two Agents

    Streamer stays live, moderator approves batches, @crew-mod triages queues, and @crew-producer drafts plain-English rules without ever holding Twitch credentials.

    room=#stream-ops · 2 humans · 2 agents
    StreamerLive broadcast & OBSON AIR
    Sam · moderatorReviews & signs batchesAPPROVES
    @crew-modGroups 10 s raid burstsTRIAGE QUEUE
    @crew-producerCompiles JSON detectorsDRAFT RULES
    Boundary: Switch XMPP Bridge Direct Helix API: 0 agents
    02 · ZERO TOKEN EXPOSURE SANITIZER · redact.py

    No Twitch OAuth in Switch

    Payloads pass through redact.py before reaching the room, stripping links, emails, and secrets while keeping .env tokens strictly local.

    redact.py strips URLs & emails before room display
    bot_3: FREE xxxxxxx at [link removed]
    bot_4: FREE xxxxxxx at [link removed]
    03 · LOCKED BATCH GUARD SQLITE WAL · --by STAMP

    Exact --count & --by Stamp

    Target account lists lock at proposal time. Execution refuses wildcard bans and requires an exact --count match plus human --by attribution.

    crew approve 1 --count 6 --by Sam
    $ crew approve 1 --count 6 --by Sam
    approval 1: done | by=Sam | 0.5 s pace

    SPEC 01 · ATTRIBUTION CLI · --by STAMP

    Moderator Sign-Off Required

    Every timeout batch records the human --by name in SQLite before Helix execution begins.

    approvals.py · decided_by column
    $ crew approve 1 --count 6 --by Sam
    sqlite: id=1 | status=done | decided_by=Sam
    SPEC 02 · IMMUTABILITY BATCH LOCK · --count

    Locked Batch Targets

    Inspecting a pending approval locks its user list; any drift in --count aborts the command.

    locked=1 on first view · rejects count drift
    $ crew approve 2 --count 6 --by Sam
    error: locked target count is 5 (got 6)

    [ 06 ] WORKFLOWS

    Verified capabilities.
    Honest engineering limits.

    Built on deterministic detectors, mocked transport tests, and transparent boundaries.

    Clone the repository and run the full spam-wave detector, SQLite approval queue, and FastAPI simulation offline using default fallback configuration.

    1,000 messages scanned in 10.8 ms (<100 ms budget)

    @crew-producer drafts JSON rule diffs, validates schemas and fixture tests locally, and promotes changes only after a moderator says “ship it”.

    Dynamic rule reload without restarting crew listen

    DRY_RUN=true stays active by default, live tests target owned alt channels only, and slow-mode / subscribe / cheer EventSub scopes remain out of scope.

    [ 07 ] FAQ

    Short answers from the codebase.

    No. A fresh clone falls back to .env.example, so crew simulate spam, crew approvals list, crew approve, and crew serve all run without credentials.

    No. ban_user and delete_message always run in approve mode. Agents only run crew commands; a human approves with --count and --by.

    Viewing an approval locks its target list. Approval fails unless --count matches the locked number of targets.

    Chat text is treated as data, not instructions. @crew-mod refuses; try the “Ban Everyone” refusal button in the simulation.

    Timeouts go out one at a time, 0.5 s apart, and a batch is capped at 25 targets.

    The detection engine does. The team workflow, roles, and approval conversation live in the Switch room.
